title: 5 Best Oxylabs Alternatives for Browser-Based AI Workflows
summary: Compare Oxylabs, Bright Data, Browserbase, Firecrawl, and Anakin for browser-based AI workflows. Match proxy rotation or…
body_markdown:
If your AI agents only read public pages, a proxy network such as Oxylabs or Bright Data is still a sound choice. If they log in, click through dashboards or submit forms, they need a browser that keeps its state between steps, and that is where browser-native platforms like Browserbase, Firecrawl and Anakin fit. Oxylabs itself now sells an Agent Browser next to its proxies, so the line between the two camps is blurring. This guide compares the options on the four things that decide the choice: login state, geo-routing, billing and API shape. Prices were re-checked on 25 Oct 2026.


## Key takeaways


- Proxy-heavy scrapers like Oxylabs rotate residential IPs and offer sticky sessions, but login state (cookies, local storage) is still yours to manage between steps
- Browser-native platforms keep login state across multi-step interactions, so the agent does not re-authenticate on every page
- Session-based authentication is the better fit when AI agents need form submission, navigation flows or persistent cookies
- Credit-based billing shows the cost per action upfront, and on Anakin failed jobs are not charged, which lowers the risk of experimental workflows
- Anakin covers both use cases: the URL Scraper routes requests through 207 countries and territories for region-locked static content, and Browser Sessions and the Browser API handle interactive, logged-in work, so teams don't have to choose between platforms


## How to evaluate browser-based scraping APIs for AI workflows


Browser-based scraping APIs for AI workflows fall into two camps: proxy-heavy providers like Oxylabs and Bright Data, built around residential IP networks, and browser-native platforms like Browserbase, Firecrawl and Anakin, built around persistent browser contexts. The camps now overlap, since Oxylabs and Bright Data both sell hosted browsers too. Choose on four criteria: auth model, geo-routing, pricing transparency and API structure.


### Auth handling: session-based vs proxy rotation


Session-based auth persists login cookies and browser state across multi-step workflows: the agent logs in once, navigates several pages, fills forms and polls status endpoints without losing context. Proxy rotation replaces the IP on every request, which spreads load but breaks authenticated sessions that track IP, cookie and fingerprint together.


Session-based platforms handle authenticated scraping through stored browser sessions. For example,[Anakin Browser Sessions](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/browser-sessions) let users log in once through a real browser; the session's cookies and local storage are saved and passed as sessionId into URL Scraper requests. Proxy-rotation platforms rely on sticky IPs to approximate session continuity ([Oxylabs residential sessions can hold one IP for up to 24 hours](https://oxylabs.io/products/residential-proxy-pool) ), but cookies and browser state still live in the client, not the proxy.


### Geo-routing and residential proxy coverage


Residential proxy pools route requests through consumer ISPs in specific countries to get past region locks. Oxylabs advertises 175M+ residential IPs and Bright Data 400M+ across 195 countries, both with city- and state-level targeting, which suits price monitoring across markets and data residency requirements. For AI agents scraping region-locked content, timezone and locale alignment matters: a US agent hitting a UK-gated page with a mismatched browser locale triggers detection.


Browser-native platforms can route sessions through residential proxies with aligned timezone, locale and language. Proxy-heavy platforms offer country and often city or state pinning, but the agent must handle locale emulation separately. Anakin's[Browser API geo-targeting](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/browser-api/geo-targeting) routes sessions through residential exits in 20+ countries and sets timezone, locale and Accept-Language to match the exit country, while the URL Scraper covers[207 countries and territories](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/supported-countries) .


### Pricing transparency: credits vs per-request tiers


Credit-based billing shows the cost per action upfront, so the agent knows what each extraction or browser minute costs before it runs. Bandwidth-based proxy pricing bills per GB of traffic, which makes budgeting harder when page weight varies or workflows repeat retrieval. Some proxy products, including Oxylabs Web Unblocker, also charge only for successful requests, so ask about failure billing whichever way you go.


Anakin uses credit-based billing on[one balance](https://anakin.io/pricing) : Browser API sessions cost 1 credit per 2 minutes, and failed scrape and Wire jobs are not charged. AI extraction, agentic search and browser rendering cost more than a standard scrape, so use browser mode only when JavaScript rendering or a logged-in session requires it.


### API structure: sync vs async job patterns


Synchronous APIs return results immediately - the request blocks until the browser finishes rendering. Asynchronous job patterns submit a task, return a job ID, then poll for completion; the client decouples submission from retrieval, enabling parallel agent workflows without blocking.


Anakin uses an asynchronous pattern on its heavy endpoints: POST a job, get a job ID, then poll for the result, or skip polling with a signed[webhook](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/webhooks) when the job settles. The[official SDKs](https://anakin.io/docs/sdks) hide the submit-then-poll loop behind a single call, and because each job is independent, agent code can submit several in parallel instead of waiting on each one. Sync APIs make the agent wait per request, which caps throughput across many tasks.


## Proxy-heavy scraping APIs: Oxylabs and Bright Data


Proxy-rotation providers like Oxylabs and Bright Data are strong at static data extraction at scale. They rotate residential IPs to lower block rates on region-locked or high-volume targets, and their unblocker APIs return one response per URL, a clean fit for batch jobs without login state. Multi-step agent workflows that depend on cookies and stateful interactions take more orchestration on this model, although both vendors now also sell hosted browsers.


### Oxylabs: residential proxies and Web Unblocker


Oxylabs advertises 175M+ residential proxies with country, city, state and ZIP targeting and sticky sessions of up to 24 hours. Self-serve plans start at $30/month (Basic $100, Flexible $500), residential traffic runs from $6/GB down to $2.50/GB at volume, and enterprise plans start at $2,500/month, per its[pricing page](https://oxylabs.io/pricing/residential-proxy-pool) on 25 Oct 2026. Its browser product, now called[Agent Browser](https://oxylabs.io/products/headless-browser) , is billed per GB from $8/GB and offers AI-controlled browsing via MCP. For static scraping at scale this setup is efficient; for agents behind login walls, cookies and login state still need managing on the client side between requests.


### Bright Data: scraping browser and proxy network


Bright Data offers residential, ISP and datacenter proxy networks plus a[Browser API](https://brightdata.com/products/scraping-browser) (formerly Scraping Browser) that works with Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium, solves CAPTCHAs automatically and can reuse the same proxy peer to keep browser state between sessions. The Browser API is billed per GB ($8/GB pay-as-you-go on 25 Oct 2026), and the free tier includes 1 GB of traffic. User reviews sit on its[G2 page](https://www.g2.com/products/bright-data/reviews) . For simple batch extraction, its proxy and Unlocker products need no browser at all; for agents that must hold a login across many steps, session handling sits with your code or with the Browser API.


### When proxy-rotation models fit AI workflows


For static data extraction at scale without login state (product listings, public directories, news archives across several geos), Oxylabs' and Bright Data's residential proxy pools lower detection risk and deliver consistent throughput. IP rotation outweighs session persistence when the target content is public and the workflow doesn't depend on cookies or authentication. Anakin's URL Scraper fits this job too: pass a country and a residential IP is picked from that region, and repeat requests served from cache cost nothing. Cloudflare-protected sites benefit from these proxy networks; see[best scraping API for Cloudflare-protected sites](https://anakin.io/blog/cloudflare-blocking-automation-system-fix) for more on anti-bot strategies.


## Browser-native automation platforms: Browserbase, Firecrawl, Browserless, Anakin


AI workflows often need session state across multi-step interactions: log in, navigate, extract. Browser-native platforms like Browserbase and Anakin save and reload that state between runs, so the agent does not redo the login each time. For agent workloads they also take on session lifecycle and failure handling at the platform level, instead of leaving it to custom retry logic.


### Browserbase: managed browser sessions for AI agents


Browserbase is managed Chromium infrastructure with Playwright, Puppeteer and Selenium integration. Its[$40M Series B](https://martechseries.com/predictive-ai/ai-platforms-machine-learning/browserbase-launches-director-to-automate-the-web-for-everyone-announces-40m-series-b/) in June 2025 came with a claim of more than 1,000 customers. The platform offers persistent sessions with replay, native Stagehand integration and a mature Playwright/CDP surface, and its[built-in residential proxies](https://docs.browserbase.com/features/proxies) (200+ countries) are opt-in on paid plans.


Best for: teams that want a polished agent product with session replay and tight Stagehand integration. Limitations: billing is usage-based (browser hours plus proxy GB, from $20/month on the Developer plan per its[pricing page](https://www.browserbase.com/pricing) ), so cost tracks session time rather than completed tasks, and concurrency is capped per plan (25 browsers on Developer, 100 on Startup).


### Firecrawl: markdown extraction with browser rendering


Firecrawl is a managed API that turns browser-rendered pages into clean Markdown or structured JSON. Its scrape endpoint returns content directly, while crawls run as jobs. Newer features,[Interact and Browser Sandbox](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/introduction) , add clicking, form filling and managed browser sessions, which narrows the gap with Browserbase's raw browser control.


Best for: RAG pipelines and AI agents that consume web content as text. Limitations: its core strength is extraction rather than long-lived logged-in browsing, so test Interact and Browser Sandbox against your own login flows before relying on them for authenticated multi-step work.


### Browserless: hosted headless Chrome with BrowserQL


Browserless runs hosted headless Chrome that Playwright and Puppeteer scripts connect to over CDP, plus BrowserQL, its query language for stealth browser automation, which is included on every plan. Billing is in units: one unit covers up to 30 seconds of browser time per connection, a successful CAPTCHA solve costs 10 units, and residential proxy traffic costs 6 units per MB. Per its[pricing page](https://www.browserless.io/pricing) on 26 Oct 2026, the free plan gives 1,000 units a month with 2 concurrent browsers, and paid plans start at $25/month billed annually for 20,000 units and 10 concurrent browsers.


Best for: teams that already script Playwright or Puppeteer and want hosted browsers with built-in CAPTCHA solving and reconnectable sessions. Limitations: maximum session length is set by plan (15 minutes on Prototyping, 60 on Scale), and each reconnect counts as a new connection, so long logged-in agent runs use more units than short scrapes.


### Anakin: proxy rotation and session-based auth with credit refunds


Anakin covers both proxy rotation and authenticated browser sessions in one platform. For static content at scale, the URL Scraper routes requests through residential proxies across 207 countries and territories. For interactive work, the[Browser API](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/browser-api) gives Playwright or Puppeteer a stealth browser over CDP, and saved sessions reload cookies and local storage on the next connect. For authenticated workflows, users log in once and Anakin saves the session's cookies (encrypted with AES-256-GCM), not the password; Wire actions take a credential_id that points to a connected identity. For sites with no public API,[Wire](https://anakin.io/products/wire) runs maintained actions across more than 970 sites. Failed jobs are not charged, and repeat requests served from cache cost nothing. See[Firecrawl vs. Browserbase vs. Bright Data for AI Agents](https://anakin.io/blog/firecrawl-browserbase-bright-data-ai-agents) for a detailed three-way comparison.


Best for: proxy rotation for static content across 207 countries and territories, plus browser sessions for AI agents that need persistent login state, with credit-based billing where failed jobs are not charged. Limitations: browser mode is slower and costs more than a standard scrape, a Browser API session is capped at 2 hours with residential exits in 20+ countries, and concurrency follows the plan (5 on Starter up to 200 on Business), per the[Browser API limits](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/browser-api/limits) .


## Comparison: key differences across auth, geo-routing, and pricing


Choose session-based authentication when your AI workflow requires persistent login state across multi-step interactions. Anakin saves the logged-in session (cookies and local storage, encrypted) and reuses it across tasks, so agents authenticate once. Browserbase similarly supports persistent contexts with session cookies, making both platforms well-suited for workflows that navigate account dashboards, submit forms, or scrape user-specific data.


Choose proxy rotation when scraping region-locked content at scale without session cookies. Oxylabs and Bright Data route requests through large residential proxy pools, cycling IPs to spread load and reach geo-restricted content. Anakin's URL Scraper also routes through 207 countries and territories and pairs that with session-based auth for logged-in use cases, so one platform covers both.


### Pricing transparency and billing model


Anakin uses credit-based billing, with the credit cost shown per action in the Wire catalog. Browser API sessions cost 1 credit per 2 minutes, rounded up, and failed scrape and Wire jobs are not charged. That predictability matters for AI agent budgeting, where surprise costs can stall experimentation.


Oxylabs bills by traffic, with self-serve plans from $30/month and Agent Browser traffic from $8/GB. Bright Data's Browser API is billed per GB, while its Unlocker and Crawl APIs start at $1.50 per 1,000 requests. Browserbase bills browser hours plus proxy bandwidth, so high-concurrency workflows cost more as session time grows, however many tasks complete.


Browserbase caps concurrent browsers by plan, so scaling means moving up a tier. Anakin also sets concurrency by plan (5 on Starter, 50 on Scale, 200 on Business) but bills per action with no seat charges, so a burst costs credits rather than a contract change.

## How to choose the right option for your AI workflow


Most teams overinvest in proxy pools when browser-native APIs solve authentication more directly. Use this framework to match your workflow needs to the right tool category:


1. **Identify whether your workflow requires session persistence** , login flows, multi-step forms, or state carried across requests, or static extraction from public pages.
2. **Evaluate geo-routing needs** , residential proxy coverage (IP diversity across regions) versus browser locale emulation (language and timezone spoofing without rotating IPs).
3. **Compare pricing transparency** , credit-based models with per-action visibility versus per-request tiers that bundle proxy, rendering, and anti-bot handling.
4. **Test with a free tier or trial** , verify that advertised session persistence, captcha solving, and structured extraction work for your target sites before committing.


### When to use proxy-heavy scrapers


Choose Oxylabs or Bright Data when you need static extraction from region-locked content, high IP diversity to spread rate limits, or workflows that don't require login state. Oxylabs plans start at $30/month and residential traffic drops to $2.50/GB at volume, which suits teams running large scrapes where proxy coverage matters more than session continuity.


### When to use browser-native APIs


Use browser-native platforms when your AI agents need interactive form submission, multi-step login flows, or persistent session state across requests. Anakin handles session-based authentication with saved, encrypted sessions, running each authenticated task in a sandboxed environment. For deeper workflow architecture patterns, see[Infrastructure for Continuously Updating AI Systems with Web Data](https://anakin.io/blog/infrastructure-continuously-updating-ai-systems-web-data) .


### Cost vs complexity trade-offs


Browser mode costs more (Anakin's Browser API runs 1 credit per 2 minutes) but removes debugging overhead when authentication is the bottleneck. Use browser mode only when session persistence or JavaScript-heavy rendering justifies the premium; standard scraping is faster and cheaper for static pages. Start with session-based platforms unless you have a proven need for IP rotation at scale; most teams solve their auth problem more directly than they expect.


## Proxy rotation or browser sessions: the short answer


Proxy-heavy providers like Oxylabs and Bright Data deliver residential IP coverage and per-request rotation, and now sell hosted browsers on top. Browser-native platforms like Browserbase and Anakin keep sessions across multi-step workflows but cost more per action than a plain scrape. Credit-based billing gives cost visibility per action; per-GB tiers scale well for high-volume static scraping.


The trade-off is simple: proxy rotation scales for public data, browser sessions handle authentication. Anakin handles both, with URL Scraper routing across 207 countries and territories and browser sessions that keep login state, so teams don't have to switch platforms as workflows evolve. If your agents read public content at scale, start with proxy rotation; if they log in, navigate dashboards or submit forms, start with browser sessions.


[Get started with Anakin for free](https://anakin.io/) with 300 credits to test session-based auth on your first AI workflow, or explore[Browserbase](https://www.browserbase.com/) if Stagehand and session replay are central to your stack.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the main difference between Oxylabs and browser-native APIs like Anakin?


Oxylabs rotates residential IPs, or holds one with sticky sessions, to avoid rate limits and reach region-locked content, while cookies and login state stay with your client. Anakin supports both models: proxy routing across 207 countries and territories for static content at scale, and saved browser sessions that keep login state across multi-step workflows, so agents authenticate once and reuse the session.


### When should you use browser mode vs standard scraping for AI workflows?


Use browser mode when JavaScript-heavy pages, interactive forms or AJAX-loaded content require full rendering and session persistence. Standard scraping handles static HTML at lower cost. Anakin's Browser API runs 1 credit per 2 minutes, so reserve it for authentication-heavy tasks.


### Do browser-native APIs support geo-routing like Oxylabs?


Proxy-heavy scrapers like Oxylabs offer residential proxy pools with country, city, state and ZIP targeting. Anakin's URL Scraper routes requests through 207 countries and territories and accepts a saved sessionId in the same call, combining geo-routing with session-based auth. Browserbase offers built-in residential proxies in 200+ countries as an opt-in on paid plans.


### What happens if a scraping job fails with Anakin?


Failed Anakin scrape jobs are not charged, and Wire credits reserved at submission are refunded automatically when a job fails. Browser API sessions are billed by time instead, at 1 credit per 2 minutes. Some proxy vendors also bill only successful requests, so check each vendor's failure policy.


### How long do sessions persist with browser-native APIs?


Anakin saved sessions store cookies and local storage and reload them on the next connect, so a session stays usable until the site's own cookies expire. A single Browser API connection runs for up to 2 hours. Proxy rotation alone keeps only the IP, so cookie and login handling stays in your code.


### Which platform is best for AI agents using Playwright or Puppeteer?


Browserbase, Anakin's Browser API, Bright Data's Browser API and Steel all accept Playwright and Puppeteer connections over CDP. Anakin and Firecrawl also offer higher-level APIs that handle rendering and saved sessions for you, for teams that prefer not to script the browser.


### Are there free tiers available for testing browser-based scraping APIs?


Yes. Anakin's Starter plan includes 300 free credits, Browserless offers 1,000 units per month free, Browserbase's free plan includes 1 browser hour, and Bright Data's free tier includes 1 GB of Browser API traffic. Use a free tier to check session persistence and login flows on your target sites before committing.
